projection_notes: All 70 source rules are compiled and accounted for; no rule is silently discarded.
Source-disabled and constant-false rules retain compiled output but emit no MappingRule candidate.
Low-confidence or behaviorally ambiguous ATT&CK mappings remain in needs_review.
All 14 medium-fit rows received a direct official-MITRE-page scope audit.
No generated Falco rule is imported by the runtime or merged into mappings.py.
Raw-JSON projection remains a Layer-1 approximation; Layer 2 owns canonical field extraction.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1078 covers abuse of existing valid credentials and explicitly includes Containers; its current detection guidance includes anomalous container service-account or kubeconfig use.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: The Falco event establishes use by an unexpected authenticated identity, but operational context is still required to distinguish compromise from an incomplete allowlist.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1610 covers deploying a container, including containers configured without normal isolation or defensive restrictions.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: The event proves the risky deployment, not a subsequent host escape.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1133 explicitly includes access through an exposed Kubernetes API that does not require authentication.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: Health, live, and readiness endpoints are excluded by the Falco condition.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1609 is scoped to executing commands inside containers through administration services; port-forward creates a network tunnel without command execution.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: No current ATT&CK Containers technique cleanly covers this event alone.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1036.005 explicitly describes creating a resource in a trusted namespace or matching a container pod or cluster naming convention.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: The Falco allowlist exclusion is necessary because legitimate system pods also use these namespaces.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.rule: Service Account Created in Kube Namespace
medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1136 covers creation of an account for persistent access and lists Containers as a supported platform.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: The event proves account creation; malicious persistence intent remains contextual.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1485 includes deletion of cloud infrastructure crucial to operations to damage availability and supports Containers.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: A single successful deployment deletion is a medium-confidence signal; intent and operational criticality remain contextual.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1485 covers destruction of data or files to interrupt availability and supports Containers.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: The successful deletion destroys stored configuration data, but impact and adversarial intent remain contextual.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1485 includes deletion of cloud infrastructure crucial to operations and supports Containers.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: Namespace deletion can cascade across resources; whether the affected namespace is operationally critical remains contextual.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1136 covers creation of accounts for persistent access and supports Containers.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: The generic creation event requires context to distinguish adversary persistence from normal administration.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1485 covers destruction of stored data to interrupt services and supports Containers.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: The rule excludes service-account tokens and kube-system; impact and adversarial intent remain contextual.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1610 covers deploying containers through container management APIs; an ECS service is the orchestration object that deploys and maintains ECS tasks.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: The event is retained at medium confidence because the compiled Falco predicate does not inspect desired task count or image content.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1578.005 covers infrastructure-level settings such as quotas, subscriptions, tenant-wide policies, and deployment regions, not application code in an existing function.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: T1648 does not cleanly establish this update event as serverless execution without execution context.

medium_fit_mitre_audit.direct_mitre_finding: T1578.005 covers infrastructure-level compute settings, not an existing Lambda function's application or runtime configuration.
medium_fit_mitre_audit.limitation: No current ATT&CK technique cleanly covers the generic configuration update event by itself.

rules.description: Match all cloudtrail events.
rules.mapping_rationale: The source explicitly disables this catch-all debug rule and it has no ATT&CK behavior.
rules.original_condition: evt.num > 0

rules.description: The CloudTrail logging has been disabled, this could be potentially malicious.
rules.mapping_rationale: StopLogging directly disables a cloud audit log.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="StopLogging" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect creation of a new trail.
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a trail is normally defensive administration and has no reliable malicious ATT&CK mapping without its configuration.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="CreateTrail" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect a console login through Assume Role.
rules.mapping_rationale: A successful console login through an assumed cloud role is use of a Cloud Account.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="ConsoleLogin" and not ct.error exists and ct.user.identitytype="AssumedRole" and json.value[/responseElements/ConsoleLogin]="Success"

rules.description: Detect a console login without MFA.
rules.mapping_rationale: A successful non-MFA console login is use of a cloud account without the expected authentication control.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="ConsoleLogin" and not ct.error exists and ct.user.identitytype!="AssumedRole" and json.value[/responseElements/ConsoleLogin]="Success" and json.value[/additionalEventData/MFAUsed]="No"

rules.description: Detect root console login without MFA.
rules.mapping_rationale: A successful root console login is high-privilege use of a Cloud Account.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="ConsoleLogin" and not ct.error exists and json.value[/additionalEventData/MFAUsed]="No" and ct.user.identitytype!="AssumedRole" and json.value[/responseElements/ConsoleLogin]="Success" and ct.user.identitytype="Root"

rules.description: Detect creation of a new AWS user.
rules.mapping_rationale: CreateUser establishes a new Cloud Account.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="CreateUser" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect creation of a new user group.
rules.mapping_rationale: A group can carry cloud roles, but group creation alone does not prove additional privileges were assigned.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="CreateGroup" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect creation of a Lambda function.
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a Lambda function establishes serverless code execution capability.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="CreateFunction20150331" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect deactivating MFA configuration for root.
rules.mapping_rationale: Deactivating the root MFA device directly modifies multi-factor authentication.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="DeactivateMFADevice" and not ct.error exists and ct.user.identitytype="Root" and ct.request.username="AWS ROOT USER"

rules.description: Detect deleting configuration to use encryption for bucket storage.
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting bucket encryption weakens data protection, but the current ATT&CK catalog has no precise one-to-one behavior for this event.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="DeleteBucketEncryption" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect deleting blocking public access to bucket.
rules.mapping_rationale: Removing public-access blocks can enable access to cloud storage, but does not itself show that data was accessed.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="PutBucketPublicAccessBlock" and not ct.error exists and json.value[/requestParameters/publicAccessBlock]="" and (json.value[/requestParameters/PublicAccessBlockConfiguration/RestrictPublicBuckets]=false or json.value[/requestParameters/PublicAccessBlockConfiguration/BlockPublicPolicy]=false or json.value[/requestParameters/PublicAccessBlockConfiguration/BlockPublicAcls]=false or json.value[/requestParameters/PublicAccessBlockConfiguration/IgnorePublicAcls]=false)

rules.description: Detect deletion of a user group.
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting a group may remove access, but the event does not establish Account Access Removal impact by itself.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="DeleteGroup" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect a new service is created in ECS.
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating an ECS service deploys and maintains containers.
rules.original_condition: ct.src="ecs.amazonaws.com" and ct.name="CreateService" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect a new task is started in ECS.
rules.mapping_rationale: RunTask or StartTask deploys a containerized ECS workload.
rules.original_condition: ct.src="ecs.amazonaws.com" and (ct.name="RunTask" or ct.name="StartTask") and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect listing of all S3 buckets.
rules.mapping_rationale: If enabled, ListBuckets is direct Cloud Storage Object Discovery.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="ListBuckets" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect setting the permissions on an existing bucket using access control lists.
rules.mapping_rationale: An ACL may enable access to cloud storage, but the event alone does not prove data access.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="PutBucketAcl" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect applying an Amazon S3 bucket policy to an Amazon S3 bucket.
rules.mapping_rationale: A bucket policy may enable access to cloud storage, but the event alone does not prove data access.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="PutBucketPolicy" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect launching of a specified number of instances.
rules.mapping_rationale: RunInstances creates new cloud virtual-machine instances.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="RunInstances" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect launching of a specified number of instances in a non-approved region.
rules.mapping_rationale: Launching resources outside approved regions is the behavior described by Unused/Unsupported Cloud Regions.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="RunInstances" and not ct.error exists and not ct.region in (approved_regions)

rules.description: Detect updates to a Lambda function code.
rules.mapping_rationale: Rejected candidate: T1578.005 covers infrastructure-level compute settings such as quotas, tenant policies, subscriptions, and regions, not modification of an existing Lambda function's code. T1648 also does not cleanly establish this update event as serverless execution without execution context.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="UpdateFunctionCode20150331v2" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Detect updates to a Lambda function configuration.
rules.mapping_rationale: Rejected candidate: despite the API name, T1578.005 covers infrastructure-level compute settings such as quotas, tenant policies, subscriptions, and regions, not an existing Lambda function's application/runtime configuration. No current ATT&CK technique cleanly covers the event by itself.
rules.original_condition: ct.name="UpdateFunctionConfiguration20150331v2" and not ct.error exists

rules.description: Match all K8s Audit Events
rules.mapping_rationale: The source macro makes this catch-all rule always false and it has no ATT&CK behavior.
rules.original_condition: kall

rules.description: Detect any request made by the anonymous user that was allowed
rules.mapping_rationale: Allowed anonymous Kubernetes API access is an externally reachable remote-service access path.
rules.original_condition: kevt and ka.user.name=system:anonymous and ka.auth.decision="allow" and not health_endpoint and not live_endpoint and not ready_endpoint

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a ClusterRoleBinding to the cluster-admin user
rules.mapping_rationale: Binding cluster-admin adds a high-privilege container cluster role to an identity.
rules.original_condition: kevt and clusterrolebinding and kcreate and ka.req.binding.role=cluster-admin

rules.description: Detect any attempt to attach/exec to a pod
rules.mapping_rationale: Kubernetes attach/exec directly invokes commands through the container administration API.
rules.original_condition: kevt_started and pod_subresource and (kcreate or kget) and ka.target.subresource in (exec,attach) and not user_known_exec_pod_activities

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a Role/ClusterRole that can exec to pods
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a role granting pods/exec adds a cluster permission that enables container command execution.
rules.original_condition: kevt and (role or clusterrole) and kcreate and ka.req.role.rules.resources intersects ("pods/exec")

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a Role/ClusterRole with wildcard resources or verbs
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a wildcard role adds broad container-cluster permissions.
rules.original_condition: kevt and (role or clusterrole) and kcreate and (ka.req.role.rules.resources intersects ("*") or ka.req.role.rules.verbs intersects ("*"))

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a Role/ClusterRole that can perform write-related actions
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a role with write verbs adds persistent cluster permissions.
rules.original_condition: kevt and (role or clusterrole) and kcreate and writable_verbs

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a namespace outside of a set of known namespaces
rules.mapping_rationale: Namespace creation alone has no defensible one-to-one ATT&CK Containers behavior.
rules.original_condition: kevt and namespace and kcreate and not ka.target.name in (allowed_namespaces)

rules.description: Detect an attempt to start a pod with a container image outside of a list of allowed images.
rules.mapping_rationale: If enabled, starting a pod from a disallowed image is direct container deployment.
rules.original_condition: kevt and pod and kcreate and not allowed_k8s_containers

rules.description: Detect an attempt to start a pod using the host ipc namespace.
rules.mapping_rationale: The event proves deployment with a weakened IPC isolation setting; it does not prove a completed host escape.
rules.original_condition: kevt and pod and kcreate and ka.req.pod.host_ipc intersects (true) and not ka.req.pod.containers.image.repository in (k8s_audit_hostipc_images)

rules.description: Detect an attempt to start a pod using the host network.
rules.mapping_rationale: The event proves deployment with the host network namespace, which ATT&CK lists as a risky Deploy Container attribute.
rules.original_condition: kevt and pod and kcreate and ka.req.pod.host_network intersects (true) and not ka.req.pod.containers.image.repository in (k8s_audit_hostnetwork_images)

rules.description: Detect an attempt to start a pod using the host pid namespace.
rules.mapping_rationale: The event proves deployment with the host PID namespace, which ATT&CK lists as a risky Deploy Container attribute.
rules.original_condition: kevt and pod and kcreate and ka.req.pod.host_pid intersects (true) and not ka.req.pod.containers.image.repository in (k8s_audit_hostpid_images)

rules.description: Detect an attempt to start a service with a NodePort service type
rules.mapping_rationale: A NodePort can expose a remote service, but creation alone does not prove adversary use of External Remote Services.
rules.original_condition: kevt and service and kcreate and ka.req.service.type=NodePort and not user_known_node_port_service

rules.description: Detect an attempt to start a pod with a privileged container
rules.mapping_rationale: The event proves deployment of a privileged container; ATT&CK T1610 explicitly covers privileged container deployment, while it does not prove a completed host escape.
rules.original_condition: kevt and pod and kcreate and any_container_privileged and not ka.req.pod.containers.image.repository in (k8s_audit_privileged_images)

rules.description: Detect an attempt to start a pod with a volume from a sensitive host directory (i.e. /proc). Exceptions are made for known trusted images.
rules.mapping_rationale: The event proves deployment with a risky host mount, an attribute explicitly covered by ATT&CK's Deploy Container detection guidance.
rules.original_condition: kevt and pod and kcreate and sensitive_vol_mount and not ka.req.pod.containers.image.repository in (k8s_audit_sensitive_mount_images)

rules.description: Detect creating/modifying a configmap containing a private credential (aws key, password, etc.)
rules.mapping_rationale: The event proves insecure credential placement, not adversary search or collection of Credentials in Files.
rules.original_condition: kevt and configmap and kmodify and contains_private_credentials

rules.description: Detect any k8s operation by users outside of an allowed set of users.
rules.mapping_rationale: Activity by an unexpected but accepted Kubernetes identity is closest to abuse of Valid Accounts.
rules.original_condition: kevt and non_system_user and not ka.user.name in (allowed_k8s_users) and not ka.user.name in (eks_allowed_k8s_users)

rules.description: Detect any ephemeral container created
rules.mapping_rationale: Adding an ephemeral container deploys a new container into an existing pod.
rules.original_condition: kevt and pod_subresource and kmodify and ka.target.subresource in (ephemeralcontainers) and not user_known_pod_debug_activities

rules.description: Detect any k8s operation by a user name that may be an administrator with full access.
rules.mapping_rationale: If enabled, use of default administrator names is closest to abuse of Default Accounts.
rules.original_condition: kevt and non_system_user and ka.user.name in (full_admin_k8s_users) and not allowed_full_admin_users

rules.rule: Ingress Object without TLS Certificate Created
rules.description: Detect any attempt to create an ingress without TLS certification.
rules.mapping_rationale: An ingress without TLS exposes a remote service, but the configuration alone does not establish adversary use of External Remote Services.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and ingress and response_successful and not ingress_tls)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a cluster role
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a ClusterRole adds reusable cluster-wide permissions.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and clusterrole and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a cluster role
rules.mapping_rationale: ClusterRole deletion changes permissions but is not necessarily an additional-role persistence action.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and clusterrole and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a clusterrolebinding
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a ClusterRoleBinding grants additional cluster-wide permissions.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and clusterrolebinding and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a clusterrolebinding
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting a ClusterRoleBinding removes permissions and is not a clean match for additional-role persistence.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and clusterrolebinding and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a configmap
rules.mapping_rationale: Generic ConfigMap creation does not identify an adversary behavior without examining its content or consumer.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and configmap and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a configmap
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting configuration data can destroy workload state and availability.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and configmap and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a deployment
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a deployment causes containers to be deployed into the cluster.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and deployment and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a deployment
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting a deployment destroys workload state and can interrupt availability.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and deployment and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a namespace
rules.mapping_rationale: Generic namespace creation is administrative activity with no precise ATT&CK Containers mapping.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and namespace and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a namespace
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting a namespace can recursively destroy the resources and data it contains.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and non_system_user and kdelete and namespace and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a role
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a role adds container-cluster permissions that can preserve or elevate access.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and role and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a role
rules.mapping_rationale: Role deletion changes permissions but is not the additional-role behavior described by T1098.006.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and role and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a rolebinding
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a RoleBinding assigns additional cluster permissions to an identity.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and rolebinding and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a rolebinding
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting a RoleBinding removes permissions and does not reliably indicate additional-role persistence.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and rolebinding and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a secret. Service account tokens are excluded.
rules.mapping_rationale: Secret creation uses the Container API but does not itself gather credentials as T1552.007 requires.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and secret and ka.target.namespace!=kube-system and non_system_user and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a secret. Service account tokens are excluded.
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting a secret destroys credential data and can disrupt dependent workloads.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and secret and ka.target.namespace!=kube-system and non_system_user and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to get a secret. Service account tokens are excluded.
rules.mapping_rationale: Retrieving a Kubernetes Secret through the cluster API is the behavior described by Container API credential access.
rules.original_condition: secret and kget and kactivity and response_successful

rules.description: Detect an unsuccessful attempt to get the secret. Service account tokens are excluded.
rules.mapping_rationale: An attempted Kubernetes Secret retrieval is attempted credential gathering through the Container API.
rules.original_condition: secret and kget and kactivity and not response_successful

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a service
rules.mapping_rationale: A Kubernetes Service is a network abstraction, not the host-level management daemon described by ATT&CK Container Service.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and service and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a service
rules.mapping_rationale: Deleting a Service may interrupt routing, but the event does not cleanly prove Data Destruction or Endpoint Denial of Service.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and service and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a service account
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a service account establishes a new identity for cluster access.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kcreate and serviceaccount and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to delete a service account
rules.mapping_rationale: Deletion changes an account but does not match ATT&CK's persistence-focused Account Manipulation behavior cleanly.
rules.original_condition: (kactivity and kdelete and serviceaccount and response_successful)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a pod in the kube-system or kube-public namespaces
rules.mapping_rationale: Placing a pod in kube-system or kube-public can make it resemble a legitimate system resource.

attack.technique_name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

rules.original_condition: kevt and pod and kcreate and ka.target.namespace in (kube-system, kube-public) and not allowed_kube_namespace_pods

rules.rule: Service Account Created in Kube Namespace
rules.description: Detect any attempt to create a serviceaccount in the kube-system or kube-public namespaces
rules.mapping_rationale: Creating a Kubernetes service account establishes a new cluster identity.
rules.original_condition: kevt and serviceaccount and kcreate and ka.target.namespace in (kube-system, kube-public) and response_successful and not trusted_sa

rules.description: Detect any attempt to modify/delete a ClusterRole/Role starting with system
rules.mapping_rationale: Role modification can add container-cluster permissions, but the same Falco rule also covers deletion, so one technique is not reliable for every match.
rules.original_condition: kevt and (role or clusterrole) and (kmodify or kdelete) and (ka.target.name startswith "system:") and not ka.target.name in (system:coredns, system:managed-certificate-controller)

rules.rule: Untrusted Node Successfully Joined the Cluster
rules.description: Detect a node successfully joined the cluster outside of the list of allowed nodes.
rules.mapping_rationale: If enabled, an untrusted node identity accepted by the cluster is closest to Valid Accounts, but the fit is indirect.
rules.original_condition: kevt and node and kcreate and response_successful and not allow_all_k8s_nodes and not ka.target.name in (allowed_k8s_nodes)

rules.rule: Untrusted Node Unsuccessfully Tried to Join the Cluster
rules.description: Detect an unsuccessful attempt to join the cluster for a node not in the list of allowed nodes.
rules.mapping_rationale: If enabled, attempted use of an untrusted node identity is closest to Valid Accounts, but the fit is indirect.
rules.original_condition: kevt and node and kcreate and not response_successful and not allow_all_k8s_nodes and not ka.target.name in (allowed_k8s_nodes)

rules.description: Detect any attempt to portforward
rules.mapping_rationale: Rejected candidate: port-forward establishes a network tunnel but does not execute a command inside a container, which is the behavior required by T1609. No current ATT&CK Containers technique cleanly covers the event by itself.
rules.original_condition: ka.target.subresource in (portforward) and not user_known_portforward_activities
